decisions.reason: As an adjustable quarter-pallet cardboard display, it fits the firm's core corrugated POS business and likely remains a useful standard solution despite the later website gap.
A cardboard shelf display with pegboard back is still close to the firm's main display portfolio, so it is more likely to be retained than withdrawn.
A standard cardboard quarter-pallet display is a core, broadly usable retail format that a large German paper-products manufacturer would usually continue to offer.
An eighth-pallet cardboard display serves a smaller but still relevant convenience and promotional niche, so it is somewhat at risk but still worth keeping.
A wooden display pallet is less aligned with the firm's paper-based core business and is more likely to be discontinued in favor of corrugated and more easily recyclable offerings.
A quarter-pallet display tailored to media products looks like a narrowing niche by 2022 and overlaps with more general cardboard display formats, making withdrawal likely.
